A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Geometry Field Splatting with Gaussian Surfels. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and the consolidated bibliography.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and view-synthesis results, component ablations, and qualitative evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results, revises benchmark and ablation scores, and adds a two-case Shiny Blender comparison.

M1.justification: The geometry-field representation, refined splatting, color blending, losses, and latent color model remain unchanged. Section 4.3 moves earlier, but its inputs and procedure are retained; revised scores do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds two selected Shiny Blender cases representing highly specular surfaces. DTU, BlendedMVS, Mip-NeRF 360, and Tanks & Temples coverage is retained, making this a limited extension of reconstruction coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the corresponding benchmark tables remain unchanged, including NeUDF in Table 1. The new Shiny Blender comparison uses the already evaluated 2DGS comparator alongside the proposed SH and latent variants.

E3.justification: V2 adds a preliminary evaluation design using two selected Shiny Blender cases, normal-map comparisons, and Chamfer distances. Existing benchmark protocols, masking and alignment rules, and ablation controls remain unchanged; no revised training procedure is documented.

E4.justification: New Figure 11 adds a targeted case study comparing 2DGS, SH, and latent color representations on highly specular surfaces. Existing component, sorting, and directional-conditioning ablations remain, with updated numerical results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 retains the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Central results are revised across Tables 1–6. DTU latent Chamfer distance changes from 0.60 to 0.58, while BlendedMVS object averages worsen from 0.58 to 0.67 for SH and 0.59 to 0.66 for latent, reversing their ordering and narrowing the advantage over baselines. Ablation and view-synthesis scores also change, and Figure 11 adds new Shiny Blender results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1.1 corrects the mathematical rationale for perspective handling: the assertion that projecting a 2D Gaussian generally preserves its Gaussian form is replaced by an efficient ray-intersection explanation. The formal theorems and rendered derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometry-field splatting, rendering accuracy, continuity, and reconstruction quality. The added specular-surface experiment supplies support without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly explains choosing a simple latent color representation to emphasize geometry and identifies richer representations as future work for highly specular surfaces. Appendix C.3 also qualifies the color-blending benefit as especially pronounced for SH.

D1.justification: Table 1 revises the reported latent-model time from 12 to 11 minutes. The implementation basis, GPU, neighbor-search settings, and Appendix B hyperparameters remain unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds twelve references, including Ref-NeuS, NeRF-Casting, UniSDF, GS2Mesh, and additional stereo and dynamic-reconstruction work. It credits related directional conditioning and reframes the stereo discussion around reflective-surface limitations. The existing research positioning is expanded locally.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose and caption edits, expands the institutional affiliation, revises the related-work paragraph, and adds short supplementary discussions and cross-references. The overall section organization and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 11, refreshes renderings and crops in existing qualitative comparisons, and removes the duplicated supplementary bibliography. Earlier Figures 11–15 become Figures 12–16. The basic figure and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Shiny Blender comparison supplies targeted quantitative and visual support for the color representation, while the corrected perspective argument and clearer research attribution improve accuracy. These are limited gains: the new evaluation covers only two selected cases, and the mixed benchmark revisions do not establish a general performance improvement.
